title: Cloudflare follow-on file delivery
description: Remembers a client address observed with a listed Cloudflare developer or tunnel hostname. A responder HTTP header raises a notice when that address has recent hostname context and the saved URI, MIME value, or Content-Disposition matches a configured pattern. TLS SNI and the HTTP record supply hostname observations.

topics.title: Load HTTP and TLS scripts under a module
topics.description: @load imports Zeek's base HTTP and SSL/TLS scripts, which provide the connection records and events used below. module CLOUDFLARE_STAGE scopes subsequent identifiers. The TLS handler reads server_name to seed hostname context; HTTP handlers save request details and evaluate response headers.

topics.title: Add a Cloudflare follow-on notice type
topics.description: export exposes the enclosed declarations to other scripts. redef enum Notice::Type += adds Suspicious_Download_After_Cloudflare_Domain to the framework's existing enumeration. The later response-header handler uses this member when a recent client hostname observation and a configured file indicator satisfy the notice conditions.

topics.title: Set sequence age and notice suppression intervals
topics.description: interval represents a duration. sequence_window and notice_suppress both default to 5mins, and &redef allows site policy to override them. sequence_window bounds the age of a usable hostname observation. notice_suppress controls repeated framework output. Separately, cf_state retains entries with a ten-minute write-expiration timer.

topics.title: Store the hostname observation as a typed record
topics.description: CFState groups an observation's timestamp, hostname, destination address, connection UID, and method. ts has type time, dest_ip has type addr, and host, uid, and via are strings. Later output reads the retained hostname and observation method; correlation selects this record by the client address used as its table key.

topics.title: Index recent seeds by client address with write expiration

ranges.code: global cf_state: table[addr] of CFState &write_expire=10mins;

topics.description: global cf_state: table[addr] of CFState maps each client IP to one observation record. &write_expire=10mins bases expiration on the last write. A later seed replaces the earlier record for that address and refreshes retention. Each worker holds its own table, and clients sharing a visible address share that correlation key.

topics.title: Add optional request context to the connection record
topics.description: redef record connection += adds cf_req_uri and cf_req_method to Zeek's connection type. Both are strings with &optional, allowing later code to test presence with ?$ before reading with $. Each new request overwrites this single connection-level URI and method pair, including on connections carrying pipelined requests.

topics.title: Lowercase the hostname and remove a trailing dot
topics.description: norm_host accepts and returns a string. to_lower(h) initializes local x. /[.]$/ matches a literal dot at the end, and sub replaces that dot with "". The returned string keeps other characters, including any :port suffix supplied in a Host value.

topics.title: Recognize exact base service names
topics.description: The function calls norm_host and compares the result with trycloudflare.com, workers.dev, pages.dev, and r2.dev. == tests exact string equality, and each matching if returns T. These names supply the hostname context for a sequence; a later eligible HTTP response header supplies the file indicator needed for output.

topics.title: Match subdomains with explicit domain boundaries
topics.description: (^|[.]) accepts the start of the hostname or a preceding dot, [.] matches literal dots, and $ anchors the service domain at the end. pattern in x searches the normalized hostname. These expressions accept subdomains of the four listed services. return F handles names outside those exact base domains and suffix patterns.

topics.title: Lowercase the saved original URI
topics.description: is_suspicious_extension takes a string named path and returns bool. to_lower(path) makes the listed extension checks case-insensitive. Its caller supplies the saved original_URI, so percent escapes and query text remain in the tested string. Each later expression searches that complete lowercased URI for a listed suffix pattern.

topics.title: Accept a listed suffix with an optional query string
topics.description: Each regular-expression test returns T on a match. [.] marks the extension dot, ([?].*)? allows a query suffix, and $ anchors the end. The listed suffixes are wsf, bat, cmd, ps1, py, js, vbs, and url. This flag contributes URI text evidence to the later response-header decision.

return F;
}

topics.description: return F supplies the result when every preceding extension test falls through. The caller also evaluates MIME and Content-Disposition indicators. Any one of the three flags can satisfy the final decision, so response processing continues through those checks after a false extension result.

topics.title: Match binary, text, and batch MIME strings
topics.description: The helper lowercases the Content-Type value and searches for selected MIME strings. Escaped slashes represent the slash within each MIME label. A hit returns T. The list includes broad labels such as application/octet-stream and text/plain, allowing generic binary or plain-text content labels to contribute a MIME indicator.

topics.title: Match scripting MIME strings and return a Boolean
topics.description: The remaining patterns search for Python, JavaScript, and VBScript MIME strings. A hit returns T; falling through all tests returns F. These unanchored searches also accept values containing parameters or surrounding text. The response handler invokes this helper for Content-Type headers and combines its result with the other indicator flags.

topics.title: Check client membership before reading seed fields
topics.description: sequence_is_live accepts an addr and returns bool. orig !in cf_state returns F for a client address lacking a retained observation. Processing continues to the age check when membership is present, making the subsequent cf_state[orig] lookup valid. Here in tests table membership; elsewhere the same keyword searches strings for patterns.

topics.title: Compare observation age with the sequence window
topics.description: network_time() - cf_state[orig]$ts subtracts timestamps to produce an interval. Ages greater than sequence_window return F; other values return T, including equality and future-dated seed timestamps. This helper leaves the entry in place. The table's write-expiration timer independently controls retention, while client address remains the correlation key.

topics.title: Replace the client address record with current context
topics.description: seed_sequence accepts typed endpoint, UID, hostname, and method arguments. The [$ts=..., $host=..., ...] initializer fills a CFState record using the table's expected value type. Assignment stores the latest observation at cf_state[orig]. via records "ssl" or "http", and the write refreshes the table entry's retention timer.

topics.title: Check nested TLS fields before reading SNI
topics.description: ssl_established receives a connection record. c?$ssl tests for its optional TLS analysis record; c$ssl?$server_name then tests for the nested SNI field. Each == F branch returns early. Processing reaches hostname normalization when both fields are present, giving the seed handler a server name from the TLS observation.

topics.title: Seed a client window from the TLS server name
topics.description: The handler normalizes c$ssl$server_name and calls the hostname predicate. A match invokes seed_sequence with the originator address, responder address, connection UID, hostname, and literal "ssl" method. Nested $ accesses obtain the endpoint addresses. The resulting client-address entry can supply context to later eligible HTTP response-header events.

topics.title: Handle an HTTP request when its analysis record is present
topics.description: http_request receives method, original_URI, unescaped_URI, and version arguments. The c?$http guard requires the connection's HTTP analysis record before processing continues. The handler then saves request details and tests the record's stored hostname. The request-line event occurs before the current request's Host header is delivered.

topics.title: Save the original request URI and method

ranges.code:
c$cf_req_uri = original_URI;
c$cf_req_method = method;

topics.description: The two assignments copy original_URI and method into the optional connection fields declared earlier. They run before the Host-presence guard, so request details are saved whenever the HTTP record is present. Later requests replace this same URI and method pair, which the response-header handler reads as connection-level context.

topics.title: Seed from the HTTP record's available hostname
topics.description: c$http?$host checks whether the HTTP record currently holds a hostname. When present, norm_host normalizes it and the service predicate can seed via="http". http_request runs before the current Host header, so the first request may reach this check with an absent field, while a reused connection may retain an earlier hostname.

topics.title: Declare local values for each response-header event
topics.description: http_header receives connection, direction, header name, and value arguments. The local addr and string declarations reserve values for this invocation. Each response header is evaluated separately. A saved URI extension can therefore be tested on several callbacks for one response, with the notice decision made during each eligible header event.

topics.title: Initialize match flags and context for each header
topics.description: Empty strings initialize uri, matched_on, and method; F initializes ext_hit, mime_hit, and disp_hit. Zeek infers their types from these literals. seed is declared as CFState and assigned after the live-sequence check. Every callback starts with fresh flags, so the final decision combines evidence collected during that header invocation.

topics.title: Select responder headers with HTTP analysis state
topics.description: is_orig identifies originator-side headers, which return immediately. The c?$http guard then requires the connection's HTTP record. topics.title: Search Content-Disposition for a listed filename fragment
topics.description: The outer condition selects content-disposition. Its pattern searches the lowercased value for filename, optional whitespace around =, an optional quote, filename text, and a listed extension fragment. The search accepts additional characters after that fragment, so a value such as a.js.txt can match. Extended filename parameters remain in their original encoded form.

topics.title: Set the disposition flag and fill empty match context
topics.description: A successful filename-pattern search enters this block and sets disp_hit=T. If matched_on is empty, fmt records the original Content-Disposition value. An existing URI description keeps precedence. The closing braces finish the pattern and header-name branches; the disposition flag then participates in the final three-way decision.

topics.title: Require at least one indicator flag

ranges.code:
if ( ! ext_hit && ! mime_hit && ! disp_hit )
return;

topics.description: ! negates each flag, and && joins the three false-flag tests. The handler returns when all three flags are F. Processing continues when URI extension, MIME, or disposition supplies at least one T value. Combined with the earlier live-sequence gate, this condition qualifies the current response-header observation for a notice.

topics.title: Read the saved method and retained seed
topics.description: c?$cf_req_method checks presence before to_upper normalizes the saved method for display. The method supplies output context for the latest saved connection request; every method value follows the same notice path.

NOTICE([
$note=Suspicious_Download_After_Cloudflare_Domain,

topics.description: NOTICE receives a record initializer whose $note selects Suspicious_Download_After_Cloudflare_Domain. $msg supplies a fixed description of the observed sequence. The call is reached after a retained hostname seed passes the age check and at least one URI, MIME, or disposition indicator matches during a responder HTTP header event.

topics.title: Format six values into notice context

$sub=fmt("client=%s seed_host=%s seed_via=%s followon_dest=%s method=%s match=%s",
orig, seed$host, seed$via, c$id$resp_h, method, matched_on),

topics.description: fmt fills six %s placeholders with the client address, seed hostname, seed observation method, current destination, saved request method, and matched_on. seed$host and seed$via read fields from the retained CFState record. This output joins the hostname observation with the current header's indicator through the shared client-address key.
